issues.claim: StepDose("Phenytoin — loading (MoHFW 2025: 15–20 mg/kg; ICMR STW 2024: 20 mg/kg)", WeightDose(15.0, 20.0, unit = "mg", per = "IV, slowly over 30 min"), note = "MoHFW: in adults, 1 g loading then 100 mg 8-hourly"); point: "MoHFW 2025, seizures: phenytoin or fosphenytoin 15–20 mg/kg slowly over 30 min; adults 1 g loading, then 100 mg 8-hourly."
issues.problem: The weight calculator presents the whole loading dose as given 'over 30 min'. At 20 mg/kg any adult over 75 kg then receives more than 50 mg/min (100 kg: 2000 mg in 30 min = 67 mg/min), above the maximum rate in the phenytoin label's boxed warning (severe hypotension and arrhythmias). The step does not mention cardiac and BP monitoring or the saline-only diluent. Fosphenytoin is written in mg/kg instead of mg PE/kg, which the fosphenytoin label names as a source of dosing errors. The released Status epilepticus protocol (NeuroEmergencies.kt) already carries 'Up to 50 mg/min' and cardiac-monitoring cautions for the same drug, so the two protocols contradict each other.
issues.correction: StepDose note: "MoHFW: in adults, 1 g loading then 100 mg 8-hourly. FDA label: no faster than 50 mg/min in adults (children 1–3 mg/kg/min or 50 mg/min, whichever is slower), so larger doses take longer than 30 min; continuous ECG and BP monitoring during and after; dilute in normal saline only." Point: "MoHFW 2025, seizures: phenytoin 15–20 mg/kg (fosphenytoin 15–20 mg PE/kg) slowly over 30 min; adults 1 g loading, then 100 mg 8-hourly. Phenytoin no faster than 50 mg/min (FDA label). Continuing seizures: see Status epilepticus." Cite the FDA phenytoin sodium injection label (DailyMed setid 035a8d4e-2063-4240-83cb-d7eebcabe301) as a new source, or reuse the existing source em-neuro-ncs-se-2012 (Table 7) from NeuroEmergencies.kt.
issues.evidence: Phenytoin Sodium Injection label (Hikma; openFDA, effective 2024-04-09, set id 035a8d4e-2063-4240-83cb-d7eebcabe301), boxed warning: "The rate of intravenous Phenytoin Sodium Injection administration should not exceed 50 mg per minute in adults and 1 to 3 mg/kg/min (or 50 mg per minute, whichever is slower) in pediatric patients because of the risk of severe hypotension and cardiac arrhythmias." "Careful cardiac monitoring is needed during and after administering intravenous Phenytoin Sodium Injection." Dosage section: "The addition of parenteral Phenytoin Sodium Injection to dextrose and dextrose-containing solutions should be avoided due to lack of solubility and resultant precipitation." CEREBYX label (Pfizer; openFDA, effective 2025-08-28), section 5.1: "Doses of CEREBYX are always expressed in terms of milligrams of phenytoin sodium equivalents (mg PE)." "Medication errors associated with CEREBYX have resulted in patients receiving the wrong dose of fosphenytoin." The cited sources give no rate cap: MoHFW 2025 p. 37 "Inj Phenytoin/Fosphenytoin – 15-20mg/kg slow over 30 minutes"; ICMR STW Head Injury "Phenytoin (20mg/kg over 30 min IV, followed by 5mg/kg in 2-3 divided doses)".

issues.claim: StepDose("Methylprednisolone sodium succinate — bolus (ICMR STW 2024)", WeightDose(30.0, 30.0, unit = "mg", per = "IV bolus"), note = "ICMR: consider only within 8 h with incomplete injury. NICE NG41, MoHFW 2025 and AANS/CNS 2013 advise against"); point: "ICMR STW 2024: MPSS 30 mg/kg bolus, then 5.4 mg/kg/h for 23 h …"
issues.problem: The calculator shows about 2100 mg (70 kg) labelled 'IV bolus' with no rate. The methylprednisolone sodium succinate label says 30 mg/kg must be given over at least 30 minutes, and reports arrhythmias and cardiac arrest after more than 0.5 g in under 10 minutes. This is a key omission in a population (cervical cord injury) already prone to bradycardia and hypotension. Neither ICMR nor AO Spine 2017 gives a rate.
issues.correction: per = "IV over at least 30 min (not as a push)"; note = "ICMR: consider only within 8 h with incomplete injury. FDA label: give 30 mg/kg over at least 30 min — arrhythmias and cardiac arrest reported after >0.5 g in <10 min. NICE NG41, MoHFW 2025 and AANS/CNS 2013 advise against". Point: "ICMR STW 2024: MPSS 30 mg/kg (over at least 30 min, FDA label), then 5.4 mg/kg/h for 23 h — consider within 8 h with incomplete injury, aware of high-dose steroid complications." Add the SOLU-MEDROL label as a source (DailyMed setid 7271310c-7764-4812-aa30-a5e90987c7a9).
issues.evidence: SOLU-MEDROL label (Pharmacia & Upjohn/Pfizer; openFDA, effective 2026-06-25, set id 7271310c-7764-4812-aa30-a5e90987c7a9), Dosage and administration: "When high dose therapy is desired, the recommended dose of SOLU-MEDROL Sterile Powder is 30 mg/kg administered intravenously over at least 30 minutes." "There are reports of cardiac arrhythmias and/or cardiac arrest following the rapid administration of large intravenous doses of SOLU-MEDROL ( greater than 0.5 gram administered over a period of less than 10 minutes )." ICMR STW Spinal Injury, Appendix IV (https://www.icmr.gov.in/icmrobject/uploads/STWs/1726645068_3_spinal_injury.pdf): "Methyl Prednisolone Sodium Succinate: 30mg/kg bolus and 5.4mg/Kg/hr x 23 hours" — no rate. AO Spine 2017 (PMC5686915) recommends a '24-hour infusion of high-dose MPSS' and gives no bolus rate.

issues.claim: timing = "DVT prophylaxis within 72 h (ICMR STW 2024)"; "ICMR STW 2024: non-ambulatory patients with deficits need DVT prophylaxis within 72 h — LMWH or fixed low-dose unfractionated heparin, for 8–12 weeks by risk."; "CSCM 2008: mechanical compression early; LMWH or unfractionated heparin once primary haemostasis is evident; start stress-ulcer prophylaxis."
issues.problem: The cited CSCM recommendation (56) lists intracranial bleeding, perispinal haematoma and haemothorax as potential contraindications to pharmacological prophylaxis. The step leaves them out while headlining ICMR's 'must receive within 72 h'. Patients with cord injury often also have a head injury (MoHFW: presume C-spine injury in every head injury), and BTF warns of intracranial haemorrhage expansion with LMWH or heparin. A doctor following the step could start LMWH within 72 h in a patient with a traumatic intracranial bleed.
issues.correction: Replace the CSCM point with: "CSCM 2008: mechanical compression early; LMWH or unfractionated heparin once primary haemostasis is evident — intracranial bleeding, perispinal haematoma or haemothorax are potential contraindications until bleeding has stabilised; start stress-ulcer prophylaxis." Optionally add "BTF 4th edition (Level III): LMWH or heparin increases the risk of intracranial haemorrhage expansion; consider it once the brain injury is stable" (cite BTF Table 1 — Deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis).
issues.evidence: CSCM 2008, Summary of recommendations, rec 56 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2582434/): "Begin low molecular weight heparin or unfractionated heparin plus intermittent pneumatic compression, in all patients once primary hemostasis is evident. Intracranial bleeding, perispinal hematoma, or hemothorax are potential contraindications to the administration of anticoagulants, but anticoagulants may be appropriate once bleeding has stabilized." BTF 4th edition executive summary, Table 1 (Deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis, Level III): "LMWH or low-dose unfractioned heparin may be used in combination with mechanical prophylaxis. However, there is an increased risk for expansion of intracranial hemorrhage." "pharmacologic prophylaxis may be considered if the brain injury is stable and the benefit is considered to outweigh the risk of increased intracranial hemorrhage." ICMR STW Spinal Injury, Appendix V: "All neurologically compromised (non-ambulatory) patients within 72 hours must receive DVT prophylaxis."

issues.step: Neurogenic shock and blood pressure targets (and the 'MAP targets differ' note)
issues.claim: "AO Spine 2024 (weak, very low-quality evidence): MAP at least 75–80 mm Hg but not above 90–95 mm Hg, for 3–7 days." Note: "AO Spine 2024 — at least 75–80 but not above 90–95 mm Hg for 3–7 days"
issues.problem: In AO Spine 2024, 90–95 mm Hg is the upper limit for active augmentation, not a ceiling. The guideline group says explicitly that a MAP that is higher without support should not be lowered. 'Not above 90–95 mm Hg' can be read as an instruction to bring MAP down, which risks cord hypoperfusion.
issues.correction: Point: "AO Spine 2024 (weak, very low-quality evidence): raise MAP to at least 75–80 mm Hg but do not actively augment it beyond 90–95 mm Hg (do not lower a MAP that is higher without support), for 3–7 days." Note: "AO Spine 2024 — augment to at least 75–80 mm Hg and no higher than 90–95 mm Hg, for 3–7 days".
issues.evidence: Kwon BK et al., Global Spine J 2024;14(3 Suppl):187S–211S (PMC10964888), abstract: "The GDG suggested that MAP should be augmented to at least 75-80 mmHg as the 'lower limit,' but not actively augmented beyond an 'upper limit' of 90-95 mmHg". Results: "while we have recommended an upper limit of 90-95 mmHg for the MAP target, we do not believe that clinicians should actively reduce the MAP in patients who were physiologically maintaining a MAP higher than 90-95 mmHg on their own."

issues.step: Anticoagulants and tranexamic acid (and the 'Tranexamic acid regimens differ' note)
issues.claim: "CRASH-3 (adults within 3 h; GCS ≤12 or CT bleed): 1 g over 10 min, then 1 g over 8 h; fewer head-injury deaths in mild–moderate, not severe TBI." Note: "CRASH-3 — 1 g over 10 min then 1 g over 8 h within 3 h, with benefit in mild–moderate TBI (RR 0.78) but not severe TBI (RR 0.99)"
issues.problem: The evidence is overstated. The trial's primary outcome (head-injury death in patients treated within 3 h) was not statistically significant (RR 0.94, 95% CI 0.86–1.02), and the mild–moderate versus severe result is a subgroup analysis; the step and the note give only the subgroup. The eligibility summary also omits CRASH-3's exclusion of major extracranial bleeding.
issues.correction: Point: "CRASH-3 (adults within 3 h; GCS ≤12 or CT bleed; no major extracranial bleeding): 1 g over 10 min, then 1 g over 8 h. Head-injury death 18.5% vs 19.8% (RR 0.94, 95% CI 0.86–1.02); by severity, fewer deaths in mild–moderate (RR 0.78) but not severe TBI (RR 0.99)." Note: replace "with benefit in mild–moderate TBI (RR 0.78) but not severe TBI (RR 0.99)" with "primary outcome RR 0.94 (95% CI 0.86–1.02); by severity, benefit in mild–moderate TBI (RR 0.78) but not severe TBI (RR 0.99)".
issues.evidence: CRASH-3, Lancet 2019 (PMC6853170), Summary — Methods: "Adults with TBI who were within 3 h of injury, had a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 12 or lower or any intracranial bleeding on CT scan, and no major extracranial bleeding were eligible." "The primary outcome was head injury-related death in hospital within 28 days of injury in patients treated within 3 h of injury." Findings: "Among patients treated within 3 h of injury, the risk of head injury-related death was 18·5% in the tranexamic acid group versus 19·8% in the placebo group (855 vs 892 events; risk ratio [RR] 0·94 [95% CI 0·86–1·02])." "The risk of head injury-related death reduced with tranexamic acid in patients with mild-to-moderate head injury (RR 0·78 [95% CI 0·64–0·95]) but not in patients with severe head injury (0·99 [95% CI 0·91–1·07]; p value for heterogeneity 0·030)."

issues.problem: Wrong page locator. MoHFW's tranexamic acid statement is on printed page 15 (PDF page 31); printed page 14 has no mention of tranexamic acid. Trauma.kt cites the same sentence correctly as p. 15.
issues.evidence: MoHFW STG Trauma 2025 (https://www.dghs.mohfw.gov.in/uploads/assets/SwQ7pJMiJepMtqfUQNUJrGOROd584XHIgipqf7gI.pdf), PDF page 31, footer '15 | P a g e': "For severely injured administer Inj Tranexamic acid (1 gram) within 3 hours of injury along with infusion for 8 hrs (1gram)". PDF page 30 (footer '14 | P a g e') contains no tranexamic acid text (checked with pdftotext).

issues.step: Neurosurgical referral, transfer and specific injuries
issues.claim: "MoHFW 2025: admit or transfer moderate TBI to a facility with definitive neurosurgical care; if none is readily available, a trained surgeon operates on mass lesions."
issues.problem: The two Indian sources disagree and the step reports only one. ICMR STW 2024, cited in the same step for surgical thresholds, says haematoma surgery and decompression are 'to be done by neurosurgeon only'. MoHFW allows a trained surgeon when neurosurgery is not readily available. A district-hospital surgeon needs to see both, but the protocol does not record the difference.
issues.correction: Append to the point: "ICMR STW 2024: evacuation or decompressive craniectomy by a neurosurgeon only." Or add a ProtocolNote: "Who operates differs: MoHFW 2025 — a trained surgeon may operate on intracranial mass lesions if neurosurgical care is not readily available; ICMR STW 2024 — surgery to be done by a neurosurgeon only." (cite ICMR_HEAD 'Surgical management in head injury'; MOH 'Ch. 7 (pp. 37–38)').
issues.evidence: ICMR STW Head Injury 2024 (https://www.icmr.gov.in/icmrobject/uploads/STWs/1726645069_2_head_injury.pdf), Surgical management panel: "Most common operation done is decompressive craniotomy with hematoma evacuation and/ or removal of large bone flap (15x12cm). To be done by neurosurgeon only". MoHFW STG Trauma 2025, Ch. 7, Intracranial mass lesions (pp. 37–38): "Relevant surgical procedure by trained specialist (Surgeon) if neurosurgical facility is not readily available".

issues.step: Note: Carbon dioxide targets differ (also step 'Raised intracranial pressure and herniation', point 4)
issues.claim: "… European 2023 — normoventilation; BTF — no prolonged prophylactic PaCO₂ ≤25 mm Hg."
issues.problem: BTF's position is understated next to ICMR's routine PaCO₂ 30–32 mm Hg in ICU care. The BTF 4th edition executive summary keeps the third-edition text: hyperventilation only as a temporising measure for raised ICP, and avoided in the first 24 h after injury, which is the casualty period. The protocol already quotes BTF third-edition text for mannitol with that label, so leaving it out here is inconsistent and hides the main conflict with ICMR.
issues.correction: Note: "… BTF — no prolonged prophylactic PaCO₂ ≤25 mm Hg (IIB); third-edition text (not evidence-graded): hyperventilation only as a temporising measure for raised ICP, and avoid it in the first 24 h after injury." (cite BTF 'Table 1 — Ventilation therapies').
issues.evidence: BTF 4th edition executive summary (Neurosurgery 2017;80:6–15), Table 1, Ventilation therapies: "Level IIB • Prolonged prophylactic hyperventilation with PaCO2 of ≤25 mm Hg is not recommended. Recommendations from the prior (Third) Edition not supported by evidence meeting current standards. Hyperventilation is recommended as a temporizing measure for the reduction of elevated ICP. Hyperventilation should be avoided during the first 24 h after injury when CBF often is reduced critically." ICMR STW Head Injury, severe head injury pathway: "Maintain PaCO2 30-32 mmHg".

issues.claim: "European 2023 (1B): intubate without delay for airway obstruction, GCS ≤8, hypoventilation or hypoxaemia; avoid hypoxaemia (1A); normoventilate (1B)." alongside "MoHFW 2025: 100% oxygen by face mask …" and "MoHFW 2025 — SpO₂ >98%, PaO₂ >100 mm Hg"
issues.problem: Recommendation 3 of the cited European guideline also suggests avoiding hyperoxaemia. The step drops that line while it gives MoHFW's 100% oxygen and SpO₂ >98% targets, so readers never see that the sources differ.
issues.correction: "European 2023 (1B): intubate without delay for airway obstruction, GCS ≤8, hypoventilation or hypoxaemia; avoid hypoxaemia (1A) and hyperoxaemia unless exsanguination is imminent (2B); normoventilate (1B)."
issues.evidence: European guideline 6th edition, Crit Care 2023;27:80 (PMC9977110), Recommendation 3: "We recommend the avoidance of hypoxaemia (Grade 1A). We suggest the avoidance of hyperoxaemia, except in the presence of imminent exsanguination (Grade 2B). We recommend normoventilation of trauma patients (Grade 1B)." MoHFW 2025 Ch. 7 (pp. 34–35): "Give 100% Oxygen by face mask"; "SpO2 > 98%"; "PaO2 > 100 mmHg".

issues.claim: "MoHFW 2025: 100% oxygen by face mask; intubate severe TBI (GCS <8 in its primary survey; all patients with GCS 3–8 in its severe TBI section)."
issues.problem: The point gives MoHFW's intubation threshold as GCS <8 or 3–8. MoHFW's general primary survey (Ch. 2) sets a higher threshold: a definitive airway if airway integrity is in doubt or GCS ≤10. The protocol already reports MoHFW's internal inconsistency (<8 vs 3–8), but a reader would wrongly conclude that MoHFW never intubates at GCS 9–10.
issues.correction: "MoHFW 2025: 100% oxygen by face mask; intubate severe TBI (GCS <8 in its head-trauma primary survey; all with GCS 3–8 in its severe TBI section); its general primary survey advises a definitive airway if airway integrity is in doubt or GCS ≤10." Add locator: cite(MOH, "Ch. 2 Airway (p. 14)").
issues.evidence: MoHFW STG Trauma 2025, Ch. 2 Initial assessment — Airway maintenance with restriction of cervical spine motion (printed p. 14): "Establish a definitive airway if there is doubt about the patient’s ability to maintain airway integrity or GCS score of less than or equal to 10". Ch. 7 (p. 35): "Perform Endotracheal Intubation in severe TBI (GCS < 8)".

issues.claim: "ICMR STW 2024 primary care: identify, immobilise (collar, spine board, sandbags), IV Ringer's lactate, group and cross-match, catheterise, analgesia, then transfer."
issues.problem: Spinal injury often comes with severe head injury, yet ICMR's Ringer's lactate is given without the counter-position that the head-injury protocol already cites. European 2023 recommends (1B) avoiding Ringer's lactate in severe head trauma. In the spinal protocol the instruction appears unqualified.
issues.correction: Append: "(European 2023 (1B): avoid hypotonic Ringer's lactate in severe head trauma — see Head injury.)" and add cite(EU, "R15") to the step citations.
issues.evidence: European guideline 6th edition (PMC9977110), Recommendation 15: "We recommend that hypotonic solutions such as Ringer’s lactate be avoided in patients with severe head trauma (Grade 1B)." ICMR STW Spinal Injury, Primary care — management: "IV Line Ringer Lactate; collect blood for grouping and cross matching; catheterise". MoHFW 2025 Ch. 2 (p. 17): "Presume all patients with head injury or maxillofacial injury to have Cervical spine injury until proven otherwise".

issues.claim: "Canadian C-spine Rule card (Stiell 2009): the rule does not apply to this patient and cannot be used to decide on imaging." (Level.Info)
issues.problem: This band covers the highest-risk patients: GCS <15, unstable vital signs, acute paralysis, known vertebral disease. It shows only a neutral 'not applicable' with no word that the spine stays protected. The sources the score already cites are explicit. NICE NG41 keeps full in-line immobilisation when consciousness is reduced, there is limb weakness, or the assessment cannot be done. MoHFW images the cervical spine in every patient with altered sensorium.
issues.correction: Meaning (keep it short enough for the 4-line panel): "Stiell 2009: rule not applicable — it cannot clear the spine. NICE NG41: keep immobilisation if consciousness is reduced or limbs are weak; MoHFW: image if sensorium is altered."
issues.evidence: NICE NG41 rec 1.4.4 (https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng41/chapter/Recommendations): "Carry out or maintain full in-line spinal immobilisation in the emergency department if any of the factors in recommendation 1.1.3 are present or if this assessment cannot be done." Rec 1.1.3 includes "has a reduced level of consciousness" and "has any hand or foot weakness". MoHFW STG Trauma 2025 Ch. 9 (p. 45): "Do cervical spine imaging in all altered sensorium patients".

issues.step: Items and band 0 'Imaging not required by NEXUS' (default state; TraumaScoresTest.nexus)
issues.claim: Five Criterion items under "Any of these present?"; Band(0.0, 0.0, "Imaging not required by NEXUS", …, Level.Low); test: check(s, emptyMap(), 0.0, "Imaging not required by NEXUS")
issues.problem: Because the score has only Criterion items, ScoreEngine.total() is never null. The sticky panel therefore shows the green 'Imaging not required by NEXUS' as soon as the page opens, before anything is assessed. The footnote 'Unticked criteria count as absent' appears only while a Choice is unanswered, so it never shows here. NEXUS rules out injury only when all five criteria are positively met. There is also no way to record a criterion that cannot be assessed (an uncooperative patient, or one who cannot report midline tenderness); NICE NG41 treats that case as positive. The Canadian rule in the same file avoids the problem by requiring an answer first. A missed cervical injury can mean cord damage, so the untouched state should not read as a rule-out. Ottawa and PERC share the pattern, but their missed-diagnosis cost is lower or their low-pretest gate is in the caveats.
issues.correction: Add a required gating Choice as the first item, e.g. Choice("assessed", "All five criteria assessed?", listOf(Option("Yes — tick any that is present below", 0.0), Option("No, or one cannot be assessed", 1.0)), section = "Before you start"). The result stays hidden until it is answered, and 'cannot be assessed' gives 'Imaging indicated by NEXUS'. Change the section label to "Any of these present (or cannot be assessed)?". Update TraumaScoresTest.nexus: assertNull(ScoreEngine.total(s, emptyMap())); check(s, mapOf("assessed" to 0), 0.0, "Imaging not required by NEXUS"); check(s, mapOf("assessed" to 1), 1.0, "Imaging indicated by NEXUS"); expectedMax becomes 6.0 and band 1 becomes 1.0–6.0.
issues.evidence: Hoffman 2000 abstract (PMID 10891516): "The decision instrument required patients to meet five criteria in order to be classified as having a low probability of injury: no midline cervical tenderness, no focal neurologic deficit, normal alertness, no intoxication, and no painful, distracting injury." NICE NG41 rec 1.4.4: "…if any of the factors in recommendation 1.1.3 are present or if this assessment cannot be done." MoHFW 2025 Figure 14 (NEXUS panel, p. 46): "Awake, alert & reliable? — NO → Possible Spine Injury". App code: ScoreScreen.kt shows the band whenever total != null, and the line "Unticked criteria count as absent." is rendered only in the t == null branch.

issues.step: Band 0 'C-spine imaging not required by the rule' (rendering)
issues.claim: "Canadian C-spine Rule (Stiell 2001): a low-risk factor is present and the patient can actively rotate the neck 45° left and right — no radiography. NICE NG41: no immobilisation or imaging if also pain free." (206 characters)
issues.problem: The band meaning appears only in the sticky result panel, which renders Text(b.meaning, style = Theme.type.caption, color = sub, maxLines = 4) with the default overflow (clip, no ellipsis). At 12 sp Inter in a column about 300 dp wide on a 360-dp phone (screen minus 12 + 18 dp padding each side), four lines hold about 180–200 characters. The safety qualifier at the end ('if also pain free', plus the thoracolumbar condition the numbers reviewer asked to add) is the part most likely to be cut silently. This is an estimate: I did not render it, because gradle may not be run.
issues.correction: Put the conditions first and keep the text ≤ ~170 characters, e.g. "NICE NG41 adds: only if pain free and no thoracolumbar risk factor (rec 1.1.7). Stiell 2001: low-risk factor and active 45° rotation both ways — no radiography." (160 characters; this also covers the numbers reviewer's rec 1.4.8 finding). Confirm with the desktop screenshot test.
issues.evidence: composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/medicalaid/app/ui/scores/ScoreScreen.kt, sticky result panel: "Text(b.meaning, style = Theme.type.caption, color = sub, maxLines = 4)"; ui theme: "caption = TextStyle(fontFamily = inter, fontWeight = FontWeight.Normal, fontSize = 12.sp, lineHeight = 17.sp …)"; panel padding ".padding(horizontal = 12.dp) … .padding(horizontal = 18.dp, vertical = 14.dp)".
